newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares soar 3.5 pct on budget expectations.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares soar 3.5 pct on budget expectations.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi bourse surged on Wednesday on the back of expectations that the federal budget for 1997/98 (April-March) would be approved by political parties despite their differences, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange sensitive index closed 25.63 points, or 3.5 percent, higher at 751.11 points.

"Reports quoting Congress party president Sitaram Kesri, saying that his party was ready to discuss the passage of the financial budget, mainly revived buying," said Shree Bhagwan Garg of brokers Means Leasing.

Brokers said resumed buying by foreign institutional investors who had deserted the market around Easter helped lift share prices. Traders said short-covering by speculators also aided the upward trend.
"Huge short-covering in blue chips by bear operators also aided the recovery," said another broker.
Hong Kong-based Star TV's mainly Indian news programme on Tuesday quoted Kesri as saying he was ready to discuss the budget's passage in parliament.
The Congress on Sunday withdrew crucial support to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who must prove his majority in parliament by April 11.
TISCO ended five rupees higher at 168.
